Afghanistan Grand Cultural & Heritage Tour Itinerary
Day 1 — Arrival & Kabul City Tour
Welcome to Afghanistan!

Upon arrival in Kabul, our professional tour guide and driver will meet you at the airport and transfer you to your hotel. After check-in, your guide will provide a brief orientation about the tour. Depending on your arrival time, breakfast or lunch will be arranged.
You will have time for currency exchange and a visit to a local tailor shop to experience traditional Afghan clothing.
Begin your Kabul exploration with Bibi Mahro Hill, home to the famous Afghan flag and offering panoramic views of Kabul.

Continue to Mandawi Bazaar and the Bird Market, followed by a walk around Pul-e-Khishti Mosque, Nadir Pashtun Wat, Chahar Chatta Bazaar, and Pul-e-Bagh-e-Omumi. Experience the atmosphere of Kabul, meet local people, and observe everyday life and traditions.
The day concludes with a visit to the historic Shah-Do-Shamshira Mosque, associated with an early legend concerning the arrival of Islam in Kabul.
Meals: Breakfast, Lunch & DinnerOvernight: Kabul
Day 2 — Kabul to Ghazni | Ancient Ghaznavid Heritage
After breakfast, depart Kabul for Ghazni on a scenic road journey of approximately three hours.
Ghazni was an important Buddhist center during the 7th century and later became the magnificent capital of the powerful Ghaznavid Empire.
Upon arrival, complete the required registration with the provincial tourism authorities and begin exploring the city.
Visit the historic Minarets of Ghazni, commissioned during the Ghaznavid period, and explore Bala Hesar Citadel, overlooking the old city.
Walk around the traditional areas surrounding the citadel, where historic mud-brick houses, local shops, and bazaars continue to reflect the character of old Ghazni.
Meals: Breakfast, Lunch & DinnerOvernight: Ghazni
Day 3 — Ghazni to Kandahar | Journey Through Southern Afghanistan
After breakfast, continue your road journey from Ghazni to Kandahar, approximately six hours.
The route takes you through Zabul Province, offering opportunities to observe traditional villages, mud-brick houses, local bazaars, mosques, and the landscapes of southern Afghanistan.
Several stops will be made along the way for photography, refreshments, and lunch.
Upon arrival in Kandahar, complete the required registration with the provincial tourism authorities.
Spend the remaining time exploring Kandahar, meeting local people, and experiencing the city’s unique culture and daily life.
Meals: Breakfast, Lunch & DinnerOvernight: Kandahar
Day 4 — Explore Kandahar | The Cradle of the Durrani Empire
After breakfast, begin a full day of sightseeing in Kandahar.
Explore the historic Char Suq, the old bazaar where four principal market streets meet at the center of the city. Discover traditional shops, markets, handicrafts, and the atmosphere of old Kandahar.
Continue to Shahidanu Chawk (Martyrs’ Square) before visiting important historical and religious landmarks.
Visit the Shrine of the Cloak of the Prophet, one of Kandahar’s most significant religious sites.
Continue to the Mausoleum of Ahmad Shah Durrani, founder of the Durrani Empire and a central figure in Afghanistan’s modern history.
Visit the Tomb of Mirwais Hotak, the influential Ghilzai leader associated with Kandahar’s independence from Persian rule in 1709.
Explore Chihilzina (Forty Steps), a historic rock-cut site overlooking the Kandahar plain, featuring inscriptions relating to the Mughal conquest.
The day concludes with a visit to the historic Red Mosque.
Meals: Breakfast, Lunch & DinnerOvernight: Kandahar
Day 5 — Kandahar to Herat | Across Western Afghanistan
After breakfast, depart Kandahar for Herat on an approximately eight-hour overland journey.
Travel through Helmand and Farah Provinces, experiencing the changing landscapes of southern and western Afghanistan.
Along the way, make several stops at scenic locations for photography, refreshments, and lunch.
Arrive in Herat in the evening and transfer to your hotel.
Meals: Breakfast, Lunch & DinnerOvernight: Herat
Day 6 — Explore Herat | City of Culture & Silk Road Heritage
After breakfast, complete the required registration with the tourism authorities before beginning your Herat city tour.
Visit the magnificent Masjid-e-Jami (Friday Mosque), one of Afghanistan’s greatest architectural treasures and a masterpiece of Islamic art and architecture.

Explore the historic old city of Herat and discover the cultural heritage of the city’s diverse communities, including the historic Jewish quarter and its remaining religious and architectural sites, where accessible.
Continue through the traditional Caravanserais around Chahar Suq, once important stopping points along the historic Silk Road.
Visit the spectacular Musalla Complex, commissioned during the Timurid period under Queen Gawhar Shad, wife of Shah Rukh.
Explore the historic Citadel of Herat, traditionally associated with Alexander the Great and later developed into its present form through successive Afghan and regional dynasties.
Continue to the shrine of Khwaja Abdullah Ansari, the celebrated Sufi poet, scholar, and philosopher associated with Herat.
Inside the complex, see the remarkable Haft Qalam Stone (Seven Pens Stone), an intricately crafted black-marble sarcophagus dating from the Timurid period.
Meals: Breakfast, Lunch & DinnerOvernight: Herat
Day 7 — Herat to Kabul by Flight | Kabul to Bamyan
After breakfast, transfer to the airport for your flight back to Kabul.
Upon arrival, enjoy lunch in Kabul before beginning the overland journey toward Bamyan.
The approximately four-hour drive takes you through spectacular mountain landscapes and the fascinating Hajigak Pass, reaching approximately 3,700 meters above sea level.
Enjoy several stops at scenic viewpoints and rest areas for photography and refreshments before continuing to Bamyan.
Arrive in Bamyan and check in to your hotel.
Meals: Breakfast, Lunch & DinnerOvernight: Bamyan
Day 8 — Bamyan & Band-e-Amir | UNESCO Heritage & Natural Wonders
After breakfast, complete the required registration with the provincial tourism authorities and begin exploring Bamyan.

Visit the Bamiyan Valley, home to the monumental niches of the famous Buddha Statues, recognized as part of the UNESCO World Heritage landscape. The Great Buddha was approximately 55 meters high, while the Small Buddha measured approximately 38 meters. Both statues were destroyed in 2001, while their historic niches remain important symbols of Afghanistan’s cultural heritage.
Continue to the ruins of Gholghola City, also known as the City of Screams, an ancient fortified settlement associated with the Ghaznavid period and later destroyed during the Mongol invasion.
In the afternoon, travel to Band-e-Amir National Park, Afghanistan’s spectacular natural landmark famous for its deep-blue lakes surrounded by dramatic cliffs.
Enjoy hiking, sightseeing, photography, and the peaceful mountain environment before returning to Bamyan.
Meals: Breakfast, Lunch & DinnerOvernight: Bamyan
Day 9 — Bamyan to Kabul | Historical Kabul
After breakfast, depart Bamyan for Kabul.

Along the way, visit the ruins of Zuhak (Red City), an ancient fortress overlooking the valley. The site is traditionally associated with the early medieval period and was later destroyed during the Mongol invasion.
Continue to Kabul and enjoy lunch upon arrival.
In the afternoon, visit Bagh-e-Babur (Babur’s Garden), the historic Mughal garden established by Emperor Babur.
Continue to Bala Hissar, the historic high fortress overlooking Kabul and one of the city’s most significant defensive sites.
The final visit of the day is Ziarat-e-Sakhi (Sakhi Shrine), an important religious and cultural landmark in Kabul.
Meals: Breakfast, Lunch & DinnerOvernight: Kabul
Day 10 — Kabul Shopping & Departure
After breakfast, enjoy your final opportunity to explore Kabul, depending on your flight schedule.

Visit Chicken Street, one of Kabul’s most famous traditional shopping destinations. Browse a wide selection of Afghan handicrafts and souvenirs, including handmade carpets and rugs, gemstones, calligraphy, miniature artworks, antiques, decorative pieces, and traditional crafts.
Enjoy lunch before our professional team transfers you to Kabul International Airport for your return flight.

After an unforgettable 10-day journey through the cultural and historical heartlands of Afghanistan, filled with ancient heritage, remarkable landscapes, local traditions, and memorable experiences, your tour with Nawi Saadi Travel & Tourism comes to an end.

Standing approximately 65 meters high, the Minaret of Jam rises dramatically from a remote valley along the Hari Rud, surrounded by towering barren mountains.

Built during the Ghurid period, the minaret is one of Afghanistan’s most remarkable surviving examples of medieval Islamic architecture. Its fired-brick structure is decorated with intricate geometric designs and an important Quranic inscription.
Enjoy hiking and sightseeing around the Minaret of Jam, taking time to appreciate its remote setting and architectural details.

7 Days of Discovery Itinerary
Day 1 — Arrival in Kabul & Kabul City Tour

Upon arrival in Kabul, our professional tour guide and driver will welcome you at the airport and transfer you to your hotel. After check-in, your guide will provide a short briefing about the tour and the days ahead.
Depending on your arrival time, we will arrange breakfast or lunch, followed by currency exchange and a visit to a local tailor shop where you can experience traditional Afghan clothing.
We then begin exploring Kabul, starting with Bibi Mahro Hill, home to the famous Afghan flag and offering panoramic views over the city.

Continue to Mandawi Bazaar and the Bird Market, followed by a walk around Pul-e-Khishti Mosque, Nadir Pashtun Wat, Chahar Chatta Bazaar, and Pul-e-Bagh-e-Omumi. These areas provide an authentic glimpse into Kabul’s daily life, local traditions, markets, and culture.
The day concludes with a visit to the historic Shah-Do-Shamshira Mosque, associated with an early Islamic legend concerning the arrival of Islam in Kabul.
Overnight: Kabul
Day 2 — Kabul to Mazar-e-Sharif by Flight
After breakfast, transfer to Kabul Airport for your flight to Mazar-e-Sharif, one of northern Afghanistan’s most important cultural and historical cities.
Upon arrival, our team will assist with registration at the relevant tourism department before transferring you to your hotel for check-in.
Visit the magnificent Blue Mosque (Shrine of Hazrat Ali), the architectural and spiritual landmark of Mazar-e-Sharif.
Later, explore the city center and traditional bazaars. Walk through Banjara Bazaar, meet local people, and experience the atmosphere, culture, and everyday lifestyle of Mazar-e-Sharif.
Overnight: Mazar-e-Sharif
Day 3 — Balkh: Journey Through Ancient Bactria
Today, travel to Balkh, one of the oldest continuously inhabited regions of the world and a remarkable center of ancient civilizations, religion, scholarship, and culture.
A short drive takes us to the historic Balkh District, where we explore some of its most important archaeological and cultural landmarks.
Visit Masjid-e-Haji Piyada (Nuh Gunbad Mosque), one of the earliest surviving Islamic monuments in Afghanistan, dating to the 9th century.
Continue to Khwaja Abu Nasr Parsa Mosque and the Tomb of Rabia Balkhi, remembered as one of the earliest and most celebrated female poets of Persian literature.
Explore the ruins of Bala Hisar-e-Balkh, traditionally associated with the ancient history of Balkh and Alexander the Great.
Visit the area associated with Mawlana Jalaluddin Balkhi (Rumi), the renowned Sufi poet and philosopher who was born in Balkh.
The tour continues to Burj-e-Ayaran, an impressive remnant of the ancient city’s defensive structures.
After exploring Balkh, return to Mazar-e-Sharif.
Overnight: Mazar-e-Sharif
Day 4 — Mazar-e-Sharif to Bamyan Overland
Today begins an unforgettable overland journey toward Bamyan, passing through some of Afghanistan’s most spectacular mountain landscapes.
The journey takes approximately 12 hours, with the route crossing the Hindu Kush and passing through the famous Salang area and mountain passes.
Continue through the beautiful Dara-e-Ghorband, following the Ghorband River and passing through Sia Gird District, traditional villages, local bazaars, and mountain communities.
There will be several stops along the way for photography, refreshments, and lunch, allowing you to enjoy Afghanistan’s dramatic scenery and rural landscapes.
Arrive in Bamyan in the evening and check in to your hotel.
Overnight: Bamyan
Day 5 — Bamyan & Band-e-Amir
After breakfast, complete the required registration with the provincial tourism department before beginning a full day of exploration in Bamyan.

Visit the Bamyan Valley and the remains of the famous Buddha Statues, once among the tallest standing Buddha figures in the world. The Great Buddha measured approximately 55 meters, while the Small Buddha measured approximately 38 meters. Both monuments were destroyed in 2001, but their niches remain an important symbol of Afghanistan’s cultural heritage.

Continue to the ancient ruins of Gholghola City, also known as the City of Screams, a historic fortified settlement associated with the Ghaznavid period and later destroyed during the Mongol invasion.
In the afternoon, travel to the spectacular Band-e-Amir National Park, famous for its extraordinary deep-blue lakes surrounded by dramatic limestone cliffs.
Enjoy hiking, sightseeing, photography, and the peaceful natural surroundings of the Band-e-Amir lakes before returning to Bamyan.
Overnight: Bamyan
Day 6 — Bamyan to Kabul & Kabul Heritage Tour
After breakfast, depart Bamyan for Kabul on a scenic approximately 4-hour journey, passing through the spectacular Hajigak Pass and surrounding mountain landscapes.
Along the route, make a stop at the historic ruins of Zuhak (Red City), an ancient fortress traditionally associated with the Hephthalite period and later destroyed during the Mongol invasion.
Continue toward Kabul with stops at scenic viewpoints for photography and refreshments.
After lunch in Kabul, visit the beautiful Bagh-e-Babur (Babur’s Garden), the historic Mughal garden associated with Emperor Babur.
Our final visit of the day will be Ziarat-e-Sakhi (Sakhi Shrine), an important religious and cultural site in Kabul.
Overnight: Kabul
Day 7 — Kabul Shopping & Departure
After breakfast, visit Chicken Street, one of Kabul’s best-known traditional shopping areas and a popular destination for visitors looking for Afghan handicrafts and souvenirs.
Browse a variety of traditional products, including Afghan handmade carpets and rugs, gemstones, calligraphy, miniature artworks, handicrafts, antiques, and decorative pieces.
Depending on your flight schedule, there may be an opportunity to visit additional attractions or markets in Kabul.
After lunch, our team will transfer you to Kabul International Airport for your return flight.

Into the Forgotten Wakhan – A 12-Day Silk Road Expedition

Journey deep into one of Afghanistan’s most remote and spectacular regions on a 12-day expedition through the Wakhan Corridor, a historic passage once connected to the ancient Silk Road. Beginning in Kabul and continuing toward the remote mountain settlement of Sarhad-e Broghil, the journey unfolds across dramatic valleys surrounded by the towering Pamir and Hindu Kush ranges.

Along the way, discover ancient fortresses, remote mountain villages, traditional Wakhi communities, and distinctive Kyrgyz nomadic settlements. Combining rugged overland travel, cultural encounters, ancient history, and breathtaking alpine landscapes, this expedition offers an extraordinary opportunity to experience the Wakhan’s isolated traditions and timeless Silk Road heritage.
